summary:
Moon Landing Guide – By Team Nesma

Moon Landing Guide is an intelligent decision-support concept designed to help evaluate and compare potential lunar landing sites.

Selecting a suitable landing location requires considering several factors, including terrain slope and roughness, solar illumination, surface hazards, and proximity to potential water-ice resources. Solar position and Earth's visibility relative to the local horizon are also important for evaluating energy availability and communication opportunities.

Our project proposes a transparent evaluation framework that combines these factors to help users understand the advantages and challenges of different lunar regions.

The prototype provides an interactive mapping workspace linked to NASA Moon Trek and access to scientific resources such as LRO, LOLA, Diviner, and the Planetary Data System (PDS).

Its main innovation is the proposed combination of multiple landing-site criteria into an adjustable decision-support approach.

Current Status: The prototype demonstrates the concept and links to NASA data resources. Automatic processing of raw NASA measurements, verified suitability scoring, solar and Earth position calculations, and historical site analysis remain future development goals.

Live Prototype: https://nesma-moon-2026.tiiny.site
details:
Moon Landing Guide is an interactive website that helps evaluate and compare Moon landing sites. The user can adjust 4 factors: Terrain Suitability, Solar Illumination, Hazard Avoidance, and Nearby Water-Ice. The website calculates a Suitability Score in real-time using a weighted formula.

We built the prototype with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. We used NASA Moon Trek for mapping, and NASA data from LRO, LOLA, and Diviner as scientific sources for our framework. We considered terrain, sunlight, Sun position, Earth visibility for communication, hazards, and water-ice proximity.

Our project is creative because it combines all these factors in one transparent tool, instead of looking at them separately. Users can change the weights for different missions, for example a solar mission prioritizes sunlight, while a science mission prioritizes water-ice.
